title: Negated Walsh character has degree at most $d$
statement: For every subset $S \subseteq [n]$ and every integer $d \ge 1$, the negated Walsh character $x \mapsto -\chi_S(x)$ has degree $\le d$. Equivalently, all of its $(d{+}1)$-fold multiplicative derivatives are trivial: for every base point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and all direction vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1} \in \{0,1\}^n$, the order-$(d{+}1)$ Gowers product satisfies $\mathrm{GP}(-\chi_S,\, d{+}1,\, x,\, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}) = 1$.
replaced: For every $S \subseteq [n]$ and $d \ge 1$, the function $-\chi_S$ has degree $\le d$.
